chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who made a bondwoman mudabbar while she was pregnant, and he said:
"If he knew of the bondwoman's pregnancy, then what is in her womb has the same status as her. But if he did not know, then what is in her womb remains in bondage."
He said: And I asked him about a man who makes a slave mudabbar while he is well-off, then later becomes needy; is it permissible for him to sell him? He said: "Yes, if he needs that."

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَتِهَا: having the same legal status as her
key_terms.دَبَّرَ: to designate a slave for emancipation after the owner's death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the fetus of a pregnant mudabbar bondwoman, and can a mudabbar slave be sold if the owner becomes needy?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on tadbir, conditional emancipation upon the owner's death. It clarifies that the ruling of a pregnant bondwoman's fetus depends on the owner's knowledge of the pregnancy at the time of tadbir, and it also permits selling a mudabbar slave if the owner later falls into need.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3460 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' asked Abu al-Hasan (as) about a man who made his bondwoman mudabbar (to be freed after his death) while she was pregnant.
Imam (as) said: "If he knew about the pregnancy of the bondwoman, then what is in her womb has the same status as her (i.e., it is also mudabbar). But if he did not know, then what is in her womb remains in bondage (not mudabbar)."
Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' further asked him about a man who made his slave mudabbar while he was financially well-off, but later he became needy.
Imam (as) said: "Yes, if he becomes in need, it is permissible for him to sell the slave."
